From Salmon quantifications to an IsoformicExperiment

Lucio Rezende QueirozIzabela Mamede Conceição

October 2, 2025

Source: vignettes/articles/isoformic-preprocess.qmd

This article goes from FASTQ files to an IsoformicExperiment with transcript-level and gene-level differential expression results. The introduction starts one step later, from ready-made tables, and the other articles analyse the object.

Quantifying with Salmon

We recommend Salmon (Patro et al. 2017) in selective-alignment mode against the GENCODE transcriptome, with inferential replicates so that swish (Zhu et al. 2019) can be used for transcript-level differential expression.

Salmon 2 is a from-scratch rewrite in Rust (2.8.0 at the time of writing). The workflow (salmon index, salmon quant, quant.sf) and the output files are the same, so read_salmon(), tximeta, tximport and swish work unchanged, but the index format is new: an index built with Salmon 1.x is rejected and must be rebuilt (the last C++ release, 1.12.0, remains available as the salmon-cpp conda package). Other changes worth knowing: selective alignment is the only mapping mode (--validateMappings is a no-op), quantification is deterministic by default (identical output for any thread count), decoy sequences no longer appear in quant.sf, and --ignoreTxVersion matches transcript identifiers without their version suffix when a gene map is given. The Salmon migration guide lists every removed or ignored option.

A typical single-sample invocation from a shell is below: --libType A detects the library type, the index is built from the GENCODE transcript FASTA with salmon index --gencode (which truncates the transcript names at the first |), --posBias --seqBias --gcBias correct the biases, --dumpEq --dumpEqWeights keep the equivalence classes and --numGibbsSamples writes the inferential replicates that swish needs into aux_info/bootstrap/.

salmon index \
  --transcripts gencode.v49.transcripts.fa.gz \
  --index salmon_index \
  --gencode \
  --threads 8

salmon quant \
  --libType A \
  --index salmon_index \
  --mates1 /path/SRR..._1.fastq.gz \
  --mates2 /path/SRR..._2.fastq.gz \
  --output /path/SRR..._quant \
  --threads 8 \
  --allowDovetail --softclipOverhangs \
  --dumpEq --dumpEqWeights \
  --posBias --seqBias --gcBias \
  --numGibbsSamples 30

The same can be driven from R through the condathis package, which installs Salmon from Bioconda into a conda environment (Linux and macOS, or WSL2 on Windows). salmon_index() and salmon_quant() run the commands above; the first call creates the environment with Salmon 2.8.0:

library(isoformic)
tx_fasta <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "fasta")
gff_path <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "gff")

salmon_index(fasta_path = tx_fasta, index_path = "salmon_index", is_gencode = TRUE, num_threads = 8)
salmon_quant(
  input_r1 = "sample_1.fastq.gz",
  input_r2 = "sample_2.fastq.gz",
  index_path = "salmon_index",
  output_dir = "quants/sample_quant",
  num_threads = 8
)

salmon_quant() draws 30 Gibbs samples per sample by default (num_gibbs = 0 skips them). Besides swish, they quantify how well the reads determine each isoform, which isoforms cannot be told apart and how confident each differential expression call is; read_salmon(inferential = TRUE) reads them and the uncertainty article explains how to use and report them.

For a decoy-aware index (recommended by the Salmon authors), build the gentrome FASTA and decoys.txt from the genome as described in the Salmon documentation and pass --decoys decoys.txt to salmon index.

Reading quantifications directly

read_salmon() reads any number of quant.sf files with DuckDB and returns an IsoformicExperiment with abundance (TPM), counts and length assays. The package ships a down-sampled dataset of six placenta samples quantified against GENCODE v49.

library(isoformic)

quants_dir <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "mini_quants")
quant_dirs <- fs::dir_ls(quants_dir, type = "directory")
names(quant_dirs) <- sub("_quant$", "", fs::path_file(quant_dirs))

col_data <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = names(quant_dirs),
  condition = factor(c(rep("control", 3), rep("treatment", 3)), levels = c("control", "treatment"))
)
col_data
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>   sample_id   condition
#>   <chr>       <fct>    
#> 1 SRR11498039 control  
#> 2 SRR11498040 control  
#> 3 SRR11498041 control  
#> 4 SRR11498079 treatment
#> 5 SRR11498080 treatment
#> 6 SRR11498081 treatment

The annotation must match the reference used for quantification, GENCODE v49 here. For real data it is downloaded once into the package cache and converted to Parquet once:

gff_path <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "gff")
annot_dir <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(gff_path)

The package bundles the subset of that annotation covering the transcripts of the mini dataset.

annot_dir <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "mini_annotation")

iso <- read_salmon(quant_dirs, annot_path = annot_dir, col_data = col_data, experiment_name = "mini_placenta")
iso
#> <IsoformicExperiment> mini_placenta
#>   annotation : gencode_v49_mini_subset (15 genes, 111 transcripts, 1,071 exons)
#>   samples    : 6 [condition]
#>   transcripts: 111 assayed from 15 genes
#>   assays     : abundance, counts, length
#>   gene assays: derived from transcript assays on demand
#>   DE results : <none>
assay_names(iso)

head(row_data(iso))

Transcript-level differential expression with swish

swish needs the inferential replicates, which tximeta imports from the Salmon output (the bundled quantifications carry them separately to keep the package small).

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(SummarizedExperiment)
  library(fishpond)
})

tximeta_coldata <- data.frame(
  files = fs::path(quant_dirs, "quant.sf"),
  names = names(quant_dirs),
  condition = col_data$condition
)
se_tx <- tximeta::tximeta(
  coldata = tximeta_coldata,
  type = "salmon",
  txOut = TRUE,
  skipMeta = TRUE,
  useHub = FALSE,
  ignoreAfterBar = TRUE,
  skipSeqinfo = TRUE
)
mini_draws <- as_inferential_replicates(
  read_parquet(fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "mini_draws.parquet"))
)
names(mini_draws) <- paste0("infRep", seq_along(mini_draws))
assays(se_tx) <- c(as.list(assays(se_tx)), mini_draws)

y <- fishpond::scaleInfReps(se_tx)
y <- fishpond::labelKeep(y, minCount = 10, minN = 3)
set.seed(20261029) # swish uses permutations
y <- fishpond::swish(y, x = "condition")

swish_results <- mcols(y) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("transcript_id")
head(swish_results)
#>        transcript_id log10mean  keep stat   log2FC    pvalue locfdr    qvalue
#> 1 ENST00000367468.10  2.923578  TRUE 1.85 1.821603 0.3115385      1 0.5785714
#> 2  ENST00000681605.1  2.553906 FALSE   NA       NA        NA     NA        NA
#> 3  ENST00000680451.1  2.350137 FALSE   NA       NA        NA     NA        NA
#> 4  ENST00000490885.6  2.225321 FALSE   NA       NA        NA     NA        NA
#> 5  ENST00000559627.1  1.959647 FALSE   NA       NA        NA     NA        NA
#> 6  ENST00000466691.1  1.607356 FALSE   NA       NA        NA     NA        NA

The results are attached to the object; tximeta objects can also be converted directly with as_isoformic(se_tx, annot_path = annot_dir).

de_tx(iso) <- swish_results
head(de_tx(iso))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 9
#>   transcript_id     log10mean keep   stat log2FC pvalue locfdr qvalue det_sig
#>   <chr>                 <dbl> <lgl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1 ENST00000263341.7      3.59 TRUE   3.25   6.63 0.0727  0.529  0.234 no     
#> 2 ENST00000651122.1      2.72 TRUE   3.5    4.91 0.0562  0.455  0.234 no     
#> 3 ENST00000306602.3      2.44 TRUE  -3.3   -3.75 0.0673  0.506  0.234 no

Gene-level differential expression with DESeq2

as_summarized_experiment() exports the gene-level assays (isoforms summed, lengths averaged by abundance) so that DESeq2 can run on them.

se_gene <- as_summarized_experiment(iso, level = "gene")
assay(se_gene, "counts") <- round(assay(se_gene, "counts"))
se_gene$condition <- factor(se_gene$condition, levels = c("control", "treatment"))

dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSet(se_gene, design = ~condition)
dds <- dds[rowSums(DESeq2::counts(dds) >= 10) >= 3, ]
dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
res <- DESeq2::results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "treatment", "control"))
shrink_type <- if (rlang::is_installed("apeglm")) "apeglm" else "normal"
res_shr <- DESeq2::lfcShrink(dds, coef = "condition_treatment_vs_control", res = res, type = shrink_type, quiet = TRUE)

de_gene(iso) <- as.data.frame(res_shr)
head(de_gene(iso))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   gene_id            baseMean       log2FC   lfcSE   pvalue  qvalue deg_sig
#>   <chr>                 <dbl>        <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>

#> 2 ENSG00000115415.22    435.   0.00000191  0.00144 0.452    0.614   no     
#> 3 ENSG00000100906.13   1212.  -0.00000132  0.00144 0.362    0.614   no     
#> 4 ENSG00000271503.7   20364.  -0.000000869 0.00144 0.477    0.614   no

Looking at the results 

top_gene <- de_gene(iso) |>
  dplyr::arrange(qvalue) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 1) |>
  dplyr::pull(gene_id)
gene_name <- gene_data(iso)$gene_name[gene_data(iso)$gene_id == top_gene]
gene_name
#> [1] "IL1B"

plot_log2fc(iso, feature = gene_name)
plot_tx_expr(iso, gene_name = gene_name, group = "condition")
plot_genomic_context(iso, gene_name = gene_name)
isoform_switches(iso) |> head()
#> # A tibble: 0 × 12
#> # ℹ 12 variables: gene_id <chr>, gene_name <chr>, gene_type <chr>,
#> #   n_tx_tested <int>, n_det_sig <int>, n_det_up <int>, n_det_down <int>,

Saving

The object, with both result tables, is written as a directory of Parquet files and restored with read_isoformic().

out_dir <- fs::path(tempdir(), "mini_placenta")
iso <- write_isoformic(iso, out_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
iso@data_path
#> [1] "/tmp/RtmpvXfAHM/mini_placenta"
fs::dir_ls(out_dir)
#> /tmp/RtmpvXfAHM/mini_placenta/assays
#> /tmp/RtmpvXfAHM/mini_placenta/col_data.parquet
#> /tmp/RtmpvXfAHM/mini_placenta/dea
#> /tmp/RtmpvXfAHM/mini_placenta/experiment.parquet
#> /tmp/RtmpvXfAHM/mini_placenta/tx_type_palette.parquet

Long reads with Oarfish

Oxford Nanopore and PacBio reads are quantified with Oarfish, which writes bootstrap replicates and a table of unique and shared reads next to the counts. read_oarfish() reads them like read_salmon() and the uncertainty functions of the uncertainty article work on them unchanged. The three samples below are simulated nanopore reads of the RBPJ transcripts, quantified with Oarfish 0.10.3 and 30 bootstrap replicates (data-raw/oarfish/), so they only show the file layout and the functions, not a real library.

oarfish_dir <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "oarfish")
prefixes <- fs::path(oarfish_dir, c("control_1", "control_2", "treated_1"))
names(prefixes) <- fs::path_file(prefixes)
fs::dir_ls(oarfish_dir, regexp = "treated_1")
#> /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/isoformic/extdata/oarfish/treated_1.ambig_info.tsv
#> /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/isoformic/extdata/oarfish/treated_1.infreps.pq
#> /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/isoformic/extdata/oarfish/treated_1.meta_info.json
#> /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/isoformic/extdata/oarfish/treated_1.quant

iso_long <- read_oarfish(
  prefixes,
  annot_path = fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "example_experiment", "annotation"),
  inferential = TRUE
)
iso_long
#> <IsoformicExperiment> isoformic_8920c3481a
#>   annotation : gencode_v33_example_subset (69 genes, 892 transcripts, 7,032 exons)
#>   samples    : 3 [oarfish_num_processed, oarfish_num_mapped, oarfish_percent_mapped, oarfish_replicate_type, oarfish_num_replicates, oarfish_optimiser, oarfish_alignment_source, oarfish_prob_model, oarfish_qc_flag]
#>   transcripts: 72 assayed from 3 genes
#>   assays     : abundance, counts, length
#>   gene assays: derived from transcript assays on demand
#>   DE results : <none>
tx_uncertainty(iso_long) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(mean_inf_rv)) |>
  dplyr::select(transcript_name, mean_count, mean_inf_rv, unique_fraction) |>
  head(6)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   transcript_name mean_count mean_inf_rv unique_fraction
#>   <chr>                <dbl>       <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1 PNCK-201             46.6         2.17         0      
#> 2 PNCK-230             18.1         1.83         0.0455 
#> 3 PNCK-203             41.9         1.76         0.00234
#> 4 PNCK-220              9.35        1.76         0      
#> 5 PNCK-223              2.49        1.69         0      
#> 6 RBPJ-205             56.2         1.64         0

The Oarfish output has no TPM, so the abundance assay is computed from the read counts and the transcript lengths. unique_fraction comes from the unique and shared read counts of .ambig_info.tsv; Oarfish has no equivalence classes, so n_classes is not available. Samples quantified by Oarfish and by Salmon cannot be read together.

In single-cell mode (--single-cell, on a transcriptome-aligned BAM whose reads carry their cell barcode in the CB:Z tag) Oarfish writes a cell by transcript count matrix and no replicates. read_oarfish_sc() sums the cells of each sample, given a table of barcodes and samples, so the isoform analyses apply to samples or to cell types (give each combination of sample and cell type its own sample_id). The example has 60 simulated cells in three samples:

sc_dir <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "oarfish_sc")
cells <- read.delim(fs::path(sc_dir, "cells.tsv"))
head(cells, 3)
#>            barcode sample_id
#> 1 CGGCGCGAACCACCTC control_1
#> 2 GTCTAGCTCGACCATC control_1
#> 3 GAAAACTGGCGGAAAG control_1
iso_sc <- read_oarfish_sc(
  fs::path(sc_dir, "out"),
  cells = cells,
  annot_path = fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "example_experiment", "annotation")
)
col_data(iso_sc)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   sample_id n_cells n_reads
#>   <chr>       <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 control_1      20   3000.
#> 2 control_2      20   3000.
#> 3 treated_1      20   3000.

Next steps

From here the object is analysed like the one of the introduction: transcriptomic diversity, isoform structure and productivity, alternative polyadenylation, enrichment by transcript type and plots. The inferential replicates imported above can be stored in metadata(iso)$inf_reps so that productive_fraction() reports the uncertainty of each fraction.
